intro: Three documents, three jobs. Know which one an employer is asking for.
rows: Short, targeted summary of your fit for one role.
Collection of work samples that proves your skills.
As many projects as needed, curated.
Design, CAD, coding, field and lab projects.
Project photos, drawings, code links, reports, results.

guides.title: Tailor it to the job or attachment
guides.body: Read the advert, pick 5 keywords, and mirror them honestly in your summary, skills and project bullets. Reorder so the most relevant items come first.

guides.title: Write a strong summary
guides.body: Two or three lines: who you are, your level and programme, your top skills, and what you want. Example: Level 300 Petroleum Engineering student skilled in CAD and data analysis seeking an industrial attachment.

guides.title: List projects and skills
guides.body: For each project give the title, your role, tools used and a measurable result. Group skills into technical, software and soft skills.

guides.title: Use action verbs
guides.body: Designed, analysed, modelled, built, tested, optimised, led, coordinated, presented. Start every bullet with one.

guides.title: Avoid common mistakes
guides.body: Typos, long paragraphs, unprofessional email addresses, vague claims without numbers, a photo or personal details that the employer did not ask for, and sending one CV to every job.

checklist: Contact details and a professional email are correct
Summary is tailored to this role
Every bullet starts with an action verb
Saved and sent as PDF with a clear file name
